contexts.text: Hence the Lord is called the shepherd of the sheep.
(Abel was) a shepherd of the flock () = one who exercises the good of charity.
He who leads and teaches is called a shepherd.... He who does not lead to, or teach, the good of charity, is not a true shepherd. Illustrated.
The foods on which his soul is fed.
He will feed them () = His presence with the regenerate.
Strife between the shepherds... ()... Shepherds of cattle = those who teach; thus the things of worship.
Shepherds of Abram's cattle () = celestial things (in worship)... Shepherds of Lot's cattle = sensuous things (in worship).
To feed in a breadth () = to teach truth.
Pastors who seduce by falsities. Treated of.
The shepherds quarrelled... () = that those who teach did not see it. Explained.
A shepherd = one who teaches these (goods and truths).
To pasture () = doctrine.
She was a shepherdess, or one who pastures () = that the affection of interior truth teaches what is in the Word. A shepherd = one who leads and teaches. Explained.
From this affection a Church is a Church, and a pastor a pastor.
Those who teach and learn are called pastor and flock.
To pasture and keep the flock () = to employ for use.
Shepherds used a rod, which = power.
(Joseph) was feeding the flock with his brethren () = to teach, in special, from doctrinal things, those in the Church.
One who pastures the flock, or a shepherd, = one who teaches. References.
To feed the flock () = to teach. AC 4709. AC 4719:end.
A shepherd, one who feeds = one who teaches and leads to the good of charity.
Joseph's brethren, being shepherds, = those who teach from faith.
Fed in the sedge () = instruction.
That to feed = to be instructed. Illustrated.

Hence it is customary to speak of feeding in relation to preaching, or instruction from doctrine or the Word; but comparatively, and not significatively as in the Word... When there is discourse (there) about instruction... meadows with flocks are represented.
Fodder is the food with which donkeys are fed.
To give fodder, which is to feed, = to instruct.
Those in internal goods of charity are called a flock, and he who leads them a shepherd.
The men are shepherds of the flock () = that they lead to good; for a shepherd = one who teaches and leads; but in the internal sense are meant the truths which lead to good. Explained. AC 6074.
Their works were to feed flocks, thus to act as shepherds: these works = goods; in special, goods from truths. Explained.
To feed () = to be instructed in truths and about goods.

Every shepherd... is an abomination to the Egyptians () = (that) perverted scientifics are opposed to the scientifics of the Church... A shepherd of the flock = one who leads to good; [and it is] the Scientific which confirms good to which the perverted Scientific is opposed. AC 6074.
God who fed me () = that Divine vivifying... To feed = to instruct.

Hence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel () = that hence is all good and truth for the Spiritual Kingdom. A shepherd = one who leads to the good of charity through the truth of faith; here, in the supreme sense, good and truth itself.
The shepherds came and drove them away () = that those who teach, being in evils, opposed themselves. Shepherds, here, = those who teach, but, being in evils, do not lead to the good of charity.
Moses was feeding the flock of Jethro () = that the law from the Divine instructed those in the truth of simple good.
To feed on wind () = to multiply a lie, ( = to imbue falsity. AE 654:58.)
The worthless shepherd who deserteth the flock () = one who teaches and leads to evil. (See AE 600:17).
As faith without charity... can yet teach... the Lord said, Feed My lambs...
I will not feed you () = not to instruct and reform.
The flock and herd shall not feed over against this mountain () = that they cannot be instructed...
Women pasturing sheep and lambs, seen.
(These priests) are good pastors of the sheep; but those who (only) teach, are evil pastors. Signified.
The Lamb... shall feed them () = that the Lord alone will teach them. AE 482.
The reason to feed = to teach. Explained, Illustrated. AE 482:2.
They said, We are pastors; we will not leave the sheep.
To pasture with an iron rod () = to teach and instruct (here, to convince) by truths from the sense of the letter. AR 828. AE 726.
Before he becomes a pastor...
(Like) a shepherd who rescues his sheep.
Such are evil pastors, and preachers.
It was pastor Wolfius.
As with the shepherds who celebrated the Lord, when born.
To feed = to instruct. References.
A true priest and good pastor...
Feed My lambs, etc. = that truth from good teaches. (Compare DWis 11. 3.)
Shepherds = those who teach truths and by them lead to good. AE 388:3. AE 601:9. AE 700:35.
Called the shepherd the stone of Israel from the doctrine of charity and thence of faith.
My shepherd () = the Lord.
Shepherds () = those who believe that they can instruct others...
Shepherds, abstractedly, = the truths themselves through which is good; thus to be without a shepherd () = no truth through which is good; thus falsity.

Shepherds = those who teach the good of life and lead to it, which is done through truths; but here () shepherds = those who do not teach the good of life, still less lead to it, because they are in falsities: this is meant by all the shepherds feeding the wind.
The Lord is called the shepherd of Israel () from the fact that He instructs and leads.
Occurs. AE 601:15. AE 701:18. AE 799:13 (depascent). AE 811:8.
Feed Thy people with Thy rod () = instruction in Divine truths...
Shepherds () = the goods of the Church; lovers, its truths.
The shepherd and his flock () = those who teach and those who learn.
In the zeal of its pastors lies hidden the fire of dominating...
Maidens as her companions (-puella pastoritia-).
